title: Allocation Horizon and Prefetch Strategy for Hierarchical KV Shards
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem summary: As request concurrency and heterogenous sequence lengths grow, our paged KV cache suffers two correlated issues: (1) high fragmentation (many partially used pages) that increases memory and copy overhead, and (2) suboptimal kernel selection for decode/prefill when KV spans are scattered across shards. This ticket proposes a combined runtime strategy: an allocation-horizon allocator that groups new KV allocations into time-bounded 'horizons', a cooperative cross-request prefetcher that prefers contiguous span reads, and a shard-aware eviction/compaction phase during low-load windows to coalesce fragments. The change touches allocator, prefill scheduler, kernel router, and metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce KV page fragmentation metric (percent partially filled pages) by >= 40% on synthetic mixed-seq workload
Improve per-request KV cache hit-rate by >= 15% for medium-length (512-2048 tokens) workloads
End-to-end median decode latency change <= +2ms and p95 <= +10ms with prefetch enabled
Kernel selector should choose contiguous-span kernel for >= 80% of prefill ops after grouping
No regressions in stability tests (stress 24h) and memory peak within 5% of baseline
design_decisions: Use an allocation-horizon model (default horizon = 10ms) to group allocations coming from closely timed prefill requests so that associated KV entries are placed into adjacent pages/shards when possible

Prefetch policy will be 'cooperative read-ahead' where the prefill scheduler calculates a reuse score per token-span (based on recent accesses, sequence length distribution, and route similarity) and issues multi-request batch reads for high-score spans
Eviction uses hybrid LRU-LFU inside each shard: evict lowest reuse-score segments first, but prefer trimming from hottest shards only when memory pressure is extreme
Introduce a low-priority compaction worker that relocates small fragments into fresh pages during <30% CPU utilization windows to amortize copy cost

Kernel selection will be guided by a simple heuristic: if span length and contiguous byte-range coverage exceed thresholds, choose contiguous-span kernel; otherwise choose scatter-gather kernel. Heuristic tunable in runtime config.
implementation_tasks: Allocator: implement horizon buckets and placement hints in kv_allocator.cc (ENG-20247-A)
Prefetcher: add reuse_score computation and multi-request coalescer in prefill_scheduler.py (ENG-20247-B)
Eviction/Compaction: low-priority relocation worker + shard-local hybrid LRULFU module (ENG-20247-C)
Kernel selector: expose contiguous-span thresholds and runtime metric hooks (ENG-20247-D)
Telemetry: add fragmentation_ratio, reuse_score_histogram, coalesced_prefetch_rate to metrics pipeline (ENG-20247-E)
E2E tests: synthetic mixed-length workload, nightlies for stress and memory (ENG-20247-F)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: aggressive prefetch can increase bandwidth and transient latency spikes. Mitigation: backpressure and prioritization; limit concurrent prefetch windows per GPU node
Risk: compaction copy operations may interfere with hot infer paths. Mitigation: compaction worker runs only when CPU and IO are below thresholds and can be cancelled if load rises
Risk: mis-tuned horizon size could increase false grouping and lower reuse. Mitigation: expose runtime flag and autosize heuristic based on observed inter-arrival distribution
Risk: kernel-selection oscillation under bursty traffic. Mitigation: hysteresis (sticky choice for N seconds) and fallbacks to scatter kernel on error
test_plan: Unit tests for allocator bucket assignment and hint propagation
Microbenchmarks: measure contiguous kernel throughput vs scatter kernel on representative NV-optimized stacks
Integration: run mixed-concurrency harness with 1k requests/sec across seq lengths {64,512,1024,2048} and collect fragmentation metrics
Canary rollout: enable on 5% of runtime nodes behind feature flag and monitor metrics for 48h
Failure injection: simulate compaction preemption and prefetch backpressure to validate safety guards
rollout_plan: Stage 1 - Feature flag implementation in runtime (no op): merge allocator and scheduler changes behind flag
Stage 2 - Telemetry only rollout to 10% to validate signals
Stage 3 - Prefetch + allocation enabled on 5% canaries; monitor overload and revert thresholds
Stage 4 - Enable compaction worker gradually in off-peak nodes, observe memory churn
Stage 5 - Gradual ramp to 100% with automated rollback if key SLOs deviate
